0.comment: Yun Jin: Shenhe and The Divine Damsel of Devastation
0.content:
"The Divine Damsel of Devastation" is a Liyue opera Yun Jin's father wrote from a Mt. Tianheng legend. In it, a brave girl volunteers to face a monster, slays it with a hidden exorcist's blade and is taken away by the adepti. During the 2.4 Jade Chamber contest Yun Jin told the tale to her new friend Shenhe, who said quietly that the real girl was probably not so brave. In an abandoned village they found Shenhe's father's diary. Shenhe was the girl, and she had not volunteered: her father had sacrificed her to a monster formed from an evil god's remains. Yun Jin offered to rewrite the opera, since she could not put her father's fiction above Shenhe's lived experience. Shenhe said she liked the opera version and hoped to grow as brave as its heroine. Yun Jin told her she had already begun.

She performed the role at the banquet on the rebuilt Jade Chamber and told Shenhe that thanks to her the tale was "more nuanced than ever". She also told her, "The play has an ending, but life goes on." Shenhe likes opera as a way of getting to know someone without talking one-on-one. She hopes Yun Jin will one day put the Traveler's story on stage. In the Hangout that followed, Yun Jin pursued the role further: she wanted to capture the damsel's fear and uncertainty, not only her heroism.

A year later Shenhe said that hearing the melody again brought back the warmth she had felt watching that performance. The opera's main aria became a song in the Fleeting Colors in Flight soundtrack, "Devastation and Redemption".

1.comment: Yun Jin: Xinyan and rock 'n' roll
1.content:
Xinyan is Liyue Harbor's rock 'n' roll musician and one of Yun Jin's closest friends. Yun Jin finds rock music full of vigor and goes to Xinyan's shows at least three times a week, however busy she is. Xinyan guesses the "finer arts" get suffocating. The troupe elders think rock is mere yelling, so Yun Jin tells them she is visiting "Xingyan", Fan Er'ye's adopted daughter, who supposedly cooks, embroiders and discusses opera. Fan Er'ye agreed to the cover story; Xingyan does not exist.

Yun Jin and Xiangling threw Xinyan a surprise birthday party in her own dark house. Yun Jin's gift was gold hairpins and iron hair ties custom-made by the Yun family; Xinyan protested that a thousand years of craft had gone into hair ties. Yun Jin once learned from Xinyan the foreign custom of making a birthday wish. In 3.4 Yun Jin coached Xinyan and Hu Tao for a Lantern Rite opening act and suggested lyrics for Xinyan's part. Afterwards she teased her for already planning the next song, and Xinyan guessed she had already named her next opera.

In 2025 Xinyan began holding concerts in Fontaine. Yun Jin left the stage to Yunning so as not to miss one, and invited the Traveler to a birthday gathering at Hotel Debord to try the local drink Fonta. In 6.3 she told the White Horse "cosplayer" that one of her friends is devoted to rock, as proof that Liyue loves more than old ways.

2.comment: Yun Jin: The Yun-Han Opera Troupe and its elders
2.content:
The Yun-Han Opera Troupe is Liyue Harbor's most acclaimed opera company and has been run by the house of Yun for generations. Yun Jin's grandfather once led it; she is now director and makes the big decisions, while managers handle daily work. Many veterans joined in her grandfather's time. They follow her lead in rehearsal but treat her like a little granddaughter offstage: no spicy food (it hurts the voice), not too much meat, more shrimp, and no rock 'n' roll. Troupe rules forbid accepting private gifts from patrons.

Her manager Yunning books interviews, keeps signed stage photos on hand for autograph-seekers and panics whenever Yun Jin vanishes. When Yun Jin went "missing" in search of inspiration, Yunning hired the Adventurers' Guild and the Traveler to find her. After a tabloid once twisted an interview into a story that she had stormed out, Yunning ruled that all press must go through her. Backstage staff include Yinggong, who handles wardrobe and props and makes paper plays for children.

In her own words, running the troupe taught her "all the highs and lows of working with people". Heyu Tea House is lenient about full costume. In 2024 two old musicians who had played for her since childhood retired and recommended successors who fit her singing at once; the change set her thinking about partings and meetings.

3.content:
Yun Jin admires Hu Tao's expressive face and sharp mind: "There's never a dull moment when you have friends like her around." Hu Tao says Yun Jin is graceful on formal occasions but surprisingly friendly in private. She once beat Yun Jin in a bet, and Yun Jin had to sing the Hilitune in operatic style.

In 3.4 (limited event) Yun Jin was a strict "mentor" to Hu Tao and Xinyan as they rehearsed a Lantern Rite act outside the funeral parlor. Hu Tao grumbled that breaks were too short for a sip of tea. In 5.3 (limited event) Yun Jin told Zhongli and the Traveler that, for all her eccentricities, Hu Tao takes pride in her work, and that her friends should simply be there when she needs them.

4.comment: Yun Jin: The Traveler, her pupil
4.content:
After the Jade Chamber contest, Yun Jin went alone to Lingju Pass to feel real danger for the divine damsel role and was so absorbed she barely noticed the monsters. The Traveler rescued her. She noted that a person who had beaten an ancient god made it impossible to feel endangered. In her Hangout she either thanks them with a night out or, when Yunning begs the Traveler to keep her busy, gives them an acting lesson. She tests their observation by counting pigeons, then has them re-enact the Jade Chamber battle. Finally she drills them with choreography against scarecrows standing in for Fatui.

She saw through the ruse from the start: it was "written on your face". She explained that all three methods (immersion, drawing on life, and rehearsed imitation) have value to her. She also admitted she had been studying the Traveler as a model for the damsel's courage. She hopes to write an opera about them one day and put them on stage. Refusing "master", "teacher" and "coach" as old-fashioned, she chose "Mentor".

In other endings the two share barbecue and a commemorative photo at Chihu Rock and Feiyun Slope. Or the Traveler asks for an autographed stage photo, which she hands over from a ready-made stack while two shopkeepers mention they own one too.

5.comment: Yun Jin: The Jade Chamber contest
5.content:
In 2.4 Ningguang offered one honest answer to the first three people who brought materials for a new Jade Chamber. Yun Jin entered because she wanted Ningguang's advice on a venue for her new opera. She reached the site on a Crux boat with Beidou and had obtained the rare stone through her father's connections. She proposed that the three parties (herself, Beidou and the Traveler with Shenhe) cooperate and share the top three places. She led the inquiry to Master Zhang of Hanfeng's Ironmongers, who had once forged stage weapons for her father, and went with the others to Mt. Tianheng for ore.

They won. Ningguang offered the Jade Chamber itself as her stage, visible from the sky and from below. When the Chamber rose, Beisht attacked; after the battle, Yun Jin performed the Divine Damsel at Ningguang's victory banquet.

6.content: Yun Jin says opera customs are passed down so faithfully that she sometimes knows the hows but not the whys. Zhongli knows the origin of almost everything: "Who wouldn't be delighted to have such a connoisseur in their audience?" In 3.4 she noted that he can appreciate Xinyan's music as well as traditional art. In 5.3 (limited event) he told her she had breathed fresh life into "The Sanctification of Tao Dou" and surpassed the original. She does not know who he really is.

7.content: The Tianquan "is a big spender" and has made several generous donations to the troupe; Yun Jin repays her with her best performances. Ningguang says she invests because elegant art forms deserve to be passed down. She gave Yun Jin the rebuilt Jade Chamber as a stage in 2.4.

8.content:
Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor thrives on two draws: storyteller Liu Su and Yun Jin's troupe. Fans wait there for her unannounced appearances, and most of the customers are said to be her fans. Owner Fan Er'ye says one of her performances brings in enough Mora to close for a month, and he likens her to Granny Ruoxin in her prime. Yun Jin loves Liu Su's "Ring of Raining Blades" and sometimes drops in just to listen. He calls her "Sir Yun" and fusses that she must rest her voice.

In 5.4 she sat by Liu Su's stall weighing whether to change lines and staging in the old classic "The Three Towers". She worried that older fans might prefer the original and that rehearsal time was short, and treated these offstage problems as part of learning to be director.

9.content: In her Hangout, a supposed Steambird editor, Boyi, ambushed her with a young journalist, Shiyun. Shiyun asked sharp questions about Yun Jin's new silk dance; Boyi wanted gossip, gifts and her opinion of the Fatui. Followed by the Traveler, Boyi turned out to run a small tabloid posing as the Steambird. He had bound Shiyun with a ruinous contract and planned to invent scandal, including gossip about her and the Traveler. In the best ending Yun Jin sent Shiyun a letter explaining that the contract's penalty was unenforceable under Liyue law. She then "kept the editor company" with polite talk of Millelith inspections until he panicked and fled, leading the Millelith, alerted by Yunning, to his base. Afterwards she admitted she is no legal expert ("acting has to be authentic to be believable") and arranged a real interview with Shiyun for the genuine Steambird.

10.comment: Yun Jin: The longevity lock and the house of Yun
10.content:
Five centuries ago the Yuns were weaponsmiths. Head of the family Yun Hui worked with Han Wu on the Prototype weapons, and his daughter Yun Huang ran the forge after him. Later generations turned to opera. Yun Jin's copper lock pendant is a forged heirloom her parents gave her after she fainted from training in the summer sun, hoping it would keep fortune and health with her. She carefully cleans it before every performance, remembering the child who trained so hard.

Her Vision came after "Snow Treading", a monodrama about a lost walker in the snow, which she first performed on a snowy day. Feeling as lost as the character, she lost herself in the role and understood that she wanted opera about true emotions. Backstage she found a Vision in her sleeve.

11.content:
- Xingqiu: a clever prankster ("Don't say I didn't warn you"). He keeps a jar of tea leaves under his bed in case her inspiration runs dry.
- Keqing: never seen at the opera and always in a hurry; Keqing says Yun Jin is why Heyu Tea House is worth every Mora.
- Kazuha: one of the many outlanders who enjoy Liyue opera; he sits quietly through every piece.
- Gaming: calls her a huge inspiration and dreams his lion-dance troupe will be half as successful.
- Yaoyao: sees her shows with Madame Ping but admits she cannot follow the lyrics.
- Xianyun: avoids operas about herself but would like to judge Yun Jin's adaptation of Shenhe's story.

12.content: Limited-time Lantern Rite events, canon but not universally known. In 2.4 (Fleeting Colors in Flight) she talked with Zhongli just before the Traveler arrived. In 3.4 (The Exquisite Night Chimes) she gave some backstage staff the festival off and mentored Hu Tao and Xinyan for the opening act. Afterwards she named her next opera "The Adeptus-Seeking Voyage". In 5.3 (Springtime Charms) she rehearsed "The Sanctification of Tao Dou" at Heyu Tea House. She explained the Three Beasts of Tao Dou to Paimon: the Lone Butterfly, the swallow Silverwing and the white horse Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare. She also explained the Lone Butterfly's sacrifice in the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array and how Old Man Wuwang carried her legacy on. After the festival she performed it again at Yilong Wharf for those who had missed it.

13.comment: Yun Jin: The White Horse poem
13.content: At the 6.3 Lantern Rite, Yun Jin was coaching storyteller Iron Tongue Tian at Third-Round Knockout when the Traveler arrived with "Ziqiao", introduced as a White Horse Adeptus cosplayer. Yun Jin explained that the text on the Lang-Gan relics, which she had been calling "An Ancient Poem", had been decoded as an ode to the moon and the White Horse Adeptus. She asked the stranger for her reading. Ziqiao explained it verse by verse. When Yun Jin introduced herself and asked her name, the stranger gave only the poem's real title, "Odes of Lang: Zibai". Yun Jin was impressed and humbled. In her 2026 birthday letter she said the legend had stayed with her, and she was writing a moon opera that everyone could help create, asking friends to send a few lines about a moon they had gazed at.

14.comment: Yun Jin: Kaeya and Klee at the opera
14.content: In a 5.4 anecdote, Kaeya brought Klee to Heyu Tea House, claiming they were on official business studying the Mondstadt wine trade. Both were enchanted by their first opera. Klee asked to learn Yun Jin's spear spinning; Yun Jin warned it was difficult but offered to teach her during the troupe's rest with a small practice spear from her childhood. Klee thanked "the kind-hearted lady who sings Liyue opera".
